about.title: Lodi Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a car part gives out on Kettleman Lane, a machine malfunctions at a Lodi warehouse, or a household item causes burns in a kitchen off Lower Sacramento Road. San Joaquin County residents deal with these injuries alongside everyday recovery, often unsure who is responsible: the manufacturer, the distributor, or the store that sold it. Under California's strict liability framework, injured people frequently don't have to prove anyone was negligent, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That said, these cases hinge on evidence, and the product itself is often the most important piece. We handle product liability claims directly for Lodi residents. Our team can evaluate what happened, identify who may be liable, and explain next steps clearly, without pressure or upfront cost.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or batteries
Lacerations from faulty tools or machinery
Crush or amputation injuries from equipment failures
Traumatic brain injuries from defective vehicle components
Poisoning or chemical exposure from mislabeled products
Choking or internal injuries from defective consumer goods

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Fight
items.desc: California often doesn't require proof of negligence in product cases — showing a defect caused the injury may be enough, which can change how a claim is approached from day one.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, and we can help sort out which parties belong in your claim.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central to proving a defect, our team works quickly to help make sure it's kept safe and properly documented.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rules often focus on whether the product itself was defective and caused harm, rather than requiring proof of carelessness. We can review your situation and explain how this may apply to your case.

items.question: What if the product was thrown away or damaged after my injury?
items.answer: It's still worth speaking with us, since other evidence like photos, receipts, or medical records may help. That said, preserving the actual product whenever possible is one of the most useful things an injured person can do.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Lodi specifically?
items.answer: Local details can matter, such as where the product was purchased or used, but California product liability law applies statewide. Our team is familiar with San Joaquin County processes and can walk you through what to expect locally.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with us?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
